blocks.content: 1. EVOLUTION OF MONEY

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: M3 (Broad Money) is the most widely used measure of money supply in India.
High Powered Money (Monetary Base) consists of currency with public plus cash reserves of banks with RBI.
Money Multiplier (m) is inversely related to the Cash Reserve Ratio (m = 1 / CRR).
Fisher's Quantity Theory establishes that the price level is directly proportional to money supply assuming velocity and output remain constant.
Keynesian liquidity preference depends on transaction, precautionary, and speculative motives.
A Liquidity Trap occurs at extremely low interest rates, rendering monetary policy ineffective.

blocks.content: The concept of money evolved to remove the inefficiencies of the barter system. Barter suffered from double coincidence of wants, lack of divisibility, absence of common measure of value, and difficulty in storing wealth.

Stages of evolution:
• Barter System
• Commodity Money (gold, silver, cattle)
• Metallic Money
• Paper Currency
• Credit Money
• Digital / Electronic Money
BARTER SYSTEM vs MONEY ECONOMY
2. FUNCTIONS OF MONEY

Primary Functions:
• Medium of Exchange
• Unit of Account
Secondary Functions:
• Store of Value
• Standard of Deferred Payment
Contingent Functions:
• Transfer of Value
• Basis of Credit
• Measure of National Income
3. TYPES OF MONEY

• Legal Tender Money – Must be accepted by law (notes & coins).
• Fiat Money – Declared by government as money.
• Near Money – Assets easily convertible into money (treasury bills).
• Digital Money – UPI, NEFT, RTGS.
4. MONEY SUPPLY IN INDIA
Money supply is measured by RBI in four aggregates:

M1 = Currency with Public + Demand Deposits + Other deposits with RBI
M2 = M1 + Savings Deposits of Post Office
M3 = M1 + Time Deposits with Banks
M4 = M3 + Total Post Office Deposits
M3 (Broad Money) is the most widely used measure in India.

cells: Currency + Demand Deposits + Other deposits with RBI

blocks.content: 5. HIGH POWERED MONEY (MONETARY BASE)
Liquidity trap occurs when interest rates are extremely low and people prefer to hold money rather than invest in bonds.
High Powered Money (H) = Currency with Public + Cash Reserves of Banks with RBI.
It is called 'high powered' because it forms the base for credit creation.
6. MONEY MULTIPLIER – COMPLETE DERIVATION
Money Multiplier (m) shows the relationship between total money supply and high powered money.
m = 1 / CRR

Example:
If CRR = 20% (0.20)
Multiplier = 1 / 0.20 = 5
If initial deposit = ₹1,000
Total money supply = 1000 × 5 = ₹5,000
Thus lower CRR → higher multiplier → higher money supply.
7. VELOCITY OF MONEY
Velocity of money refers to the frequency with which a unit of money circulates in an economy.

rows: Functions as a universal medium of exchange
Absence of common measure of value
Acts as a standard unit of account
Serves as an efficient store of value

blocks.content: Fisher’s Equation of Exchange: MV = PT
Where M = Money Supply, V = Velocity, P = Price Level, T = Transactions.
If V increases, economic activity increases.
8. FISHER’S QUANTITY THEORY
Fisher argued that price level is directly proportional to money supply assuming velocity and output constant.
MV = PT
Increase in M → Increase in P (Inflation).
9. KEYNES’ LIQUIDITY PREFERENCE THEORY
Keynes stated that demand for money depends on three motives:

• Transaction Motive (depends on income)
• Precautionary Motive (depends on income)
• Speculative Motive (depends on interest rate)
Total Demand for Money = L1(Y) + L2(r)

cells: To take advantage of interest rate changes

blocks.content: When interest rate falls, speculative demand increases.

items: M3 is officially designated as 'Broad Money' and is the most frequently tested RBI money supply aggregate.
High Powered Money (H) forms the foundation for bank credit creation in an economy.
Lower CRR directly leads to a higher money multiplier and increased total money supply.
Monetary policy becomes completely ineffective during a Liquidity Trap.

blocks.content: 10. LIQUIDITY TRAP
Liquidity trap occurs when interest rates are extremely low and people prefer to hold money rather than invest in bonds. In such a situation, monetary policy becomes ineffective.
11. MONEY MARKET EQUILIBRIUM
Equilibrium occurs when Money Demand equals Money Supply. The intersection determines equilibrium interest rate.
12. ROLE OF RBI IN CONTROLLING MONEY SUPPLY

RBI controls money supply through:
• Repo Rate
• Reverse Repo Rate
• CRR
• SLR
• Open Market Operations
13. RRB HIGH-VALUE POINTS

• M3 = Broad Money
• High Powered Money = Monetary Base
• Money Multiplier = 1/CRR
• MV = PT (Fisher)
• Liquidity Trap at low interest rate
